title: Uniform Tor bound for compactly supported direct images
statement: Work in the standing scheme setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]: $k$ is a field of characteristic $p>0$, $\ell\ne p$ is prime, and $X,Y$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism, separated of finite type, whose geometric fibres have dimension at most $d\in\mathbf Z_{\geq0}$ [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $A$ be a finite commutative discrete ring killed by a power of $\ell$, regarded as the constant coefficient ring on the small etale and pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules]. Use $\Dctf$ and Tor amplitude as in [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], with the finite discrete comparison of [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]. For integers $a\leq b$, if $M\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, then $Rf_!M\in\Dctf(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b+2d]$. Here $Rf_!$ is the compactification functor $Rp_*j_!$ for $f=pj$ [def-weil-pbc-projection-compactification], on the etale-origin objects specified by the comparison. In particular, fix a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. If a coefficient tower $C_\bullet$ has levels $C_n\in\Dctf(X_{\mathrm{proet}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)$, $n\geq1$, of common Tor amplitude $[a,b]$ [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers], then the levels of $Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet$ [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] have common Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$ and cohomology vanishing outside that same interval.

proof.text: A finite ring is Noetherian since an ascending chain of ideals is an ascending chain of subsets of its finite underlying set. Thus [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian] gives an etale representative $M'$ of $M$ with the same Tor interval $[a,b]$. Its qcqs hypothesis holds: a field is Noetherian, $X,Y$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and are quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Choose a compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{r}Y$ by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Properness of $r$ includes finite type, so $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$ and is Noetherian as well. The open part is quasi-compact by [lemma-nagata-open-immersion-qc-over-separated-target], applied to $X\to\overline X\to Y$. Compute the etale compact-support candidate $H=Rr_*j_!$ as in [def-amb-etale-compact-support].

source.place: First paragraph: reduce the finite discrete coefficient problem to its etale representative and fix a compactification

proof.text: Extension by zero is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and preserves constructible sheaves by [lem-fin-extension-by-zero]. Hence $j_!M'$ is bounded constructible: its cohomology is $j_!\mathcal H^q(M')$, in the same finite range. Apply [lem-fin-proper-bounded-constructible] to the proper map $r$ between finite-type $k$-schemes. Its coefficient hypothesis is satisfied because $A$ is finite commutative and is killed by an invertible power of $\ell$. We obtain $HM'\in D^b_c(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. The coherent compactification comparisons of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] identify this candidate with $Rf_!$ on bounded-below etale complexes.

source.place: First paragraph: establish bounded constructibility independently of the numerical Tor bound

proof.text: By [lem-sf-etale-flat-model], choose $M'\simeq P$ with $P$ a complex of flat etale $A$-module sheaves supported in $[a,b]$. It is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site]. Let $N$ be an arbitrary degree-zero etale $A$-module sheaf on $Y$, with no constructibility, finiteness or flatness requirement. The exact constant-coefficient inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes $f^{-1}N$ a sheaf in degree zero. By the K-flat definition of derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], $M'\otimes_A^L f^{-1}N$ is represented by $P\otimes_A f^{-1}N$, whose terms are zero outside $[a,b]$. Thus this tensor complex has cohomology only in $[a,b]$.

source.place: Second paragraph: the tensor test complex has the original interval [a,b]

proof.text:
We need the projection formula for this arbitrary test sheaf, rather than a formula restricted to finite-Tor constructible second inputs. For sheaves $F$ on $X$ and $G$ on $\overline X$, the adjunction $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ gives the natural map $j_!(F\otimes_A j^{-1}G)\to(j_!F)\otimes_A G$, adjoint to the identity after restriction to $X$. It is an isomorphism: using [lem-kun-stalk-as-pullback] and [lem-cbc-extension-zero-base-change], its geometric stalk is the tensor identity on $X$, and is $0\to0$ off $X$; [lem-pod-etale-stalk-tensor-scalar] computes these tensors and [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] detects the isomorphism. This sheaf tensor identity extends to $P$ and any complex $Q$ by totalization: in each total degree only the finitely many degrees of $P$ contribute, and the additive exact functor $j_!$ commutes with those finite sums. Naturality with the two differentials preserves $d_P\otimes1+(-1)^q1\otimes d_Q$. If $Q$ is acyclic, $j^{-1}Q$ is acyclic by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], so $P\otimes_A j^{-1}Q$ is acyclic by K-flatness of $P$. Exactness of $j_!$ shows that $(j_!P)\otimes_A Q$ is acyclic. Thus $j_!P$ is K-flat, and represents $j_!M'$. The preceding sheaf tensor identity applied termwise, with $G=r^{-1}N$, yields $(j_!M')\otimes_A^L r^{-1}N\simeq j_!(M'\otimes_A^L f^{-1}N)$. Apply the proper projection theorem [lem-kun-0f0g] to $r$, $E=j_!M'$ and $K=N[0]$; it allows a torsion ring and arbitrary derived inputs. It gives the well-typed isomorphism
$$HM'\otimes_A^L N\simeq H(M'\otimes_A^L f^{-1}N).$$

source.place: First paragraph: expand the compact-support projection formula with an arbitrary test module; the proper part is Stacks Tag 0F0G

proof.text: For every etale $A$-module sheaf $F$, [lem-dg-compact-support-amplitude] gives $\mathcal H^q(HF)=0$ for $q>2d$; all its hypotheses hold for $f$, including the bound on its own geometric fibres, not on the fibres of the chosen proper compactification. Negative degrees vanish: [lem-weil-pbc-dplus-injective-representative] gives an injective K-injective representative of $j_!F$ with terms zero in negative degrees, and applying $r_*$ leaves those terms zero. To pass to any complex $B$ with cohomology in $[a,b]$, use the finite truncation triangles $\tau_{\le t-1}B\to\tau_{\le t}B\to\mathcal H^t(B)[-t]\to$ of [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category], for $t=a,\ldots,b$. These triangles follow directly from the displayed good truncation complexes in that definition: the quotient of $\tau_{\le t}B$ by $\tau_{\le t-1}B$ has only $\mathcal H^t(B)$ as cohomology, in degree $t$, so its natural map to $\mathcal H^t(B)[-t]$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The starting object $\tau_{\le a-1}B$ is acyclic and hence zero in the derived category. By [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-direct-image-triangulated], $H=Rr_*j_!$ carries these to distinguished triangles and commutes with shifts. The sheaf term $H(\mathcal H^t(B))[-t]$ has cohomology in $[t,t+2d]$. Inductively the long exact cohomology sequence [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact] places $H\tau_{\le t}B$ in $[a,t+2d]$: outside this interval both neighbouring groups are zero. At $t=b$, this gives $HB$ in $[a,b+2d]$. Apply this to the tensor complex of Step 3 and use Step 4. Since $N$ was arbitrary, $HM'$ has Tor amplitude $[a,b+2d]$. This finite-truncation argument writes out the bounded hypercohomology argument in the blueprint.

source.place: Second paragraph: the fibre compact-support [0,2d] bound and the finite hypercohomology filtration

proof.text:
Return to the pro-etale category. Apply [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison] degreewise to a representative of $M'$ and use [prop-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image] for the proper, hence qcqs, map $r$. Since extension by zero preserves the lower bound, its input to the direct-image comparison is in $D^+$. These natural isomorphisms give
$$\nu_Y^*HM'\simeq Rr_{*,\mathrm{proet}}j_{!,\mathrm{proet}}\nu_X^*M'\simeq Rf_!M.$$
By Step 2, $HM'$ is bounded constructible, and by Step 5 it has the asserted Tor interval. The equivalence and interval comparison of [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian], now on the qcqs scheme $Y$, show that $Rf_!M$ is bounded constructible of that same Tor interval. This never tests an arbitrary pro-etale sheaf for vanishing using only geometric points.

source.place: First paragraph: interpret the stalk argument on etale representatives and transport the resulting Tor bound

proof.text: By the coefficient description [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], choose a uniformizer $\varpi_E$ and write $\ell=u\varpi_E^e$ with $u$ a unit and $e\geq1$. Then $(\ell^n)=(\varpi_E^{en})$, so $A_n=\mathcal O_E/\ell^n$ is the finite ring $A_{E,en}$, killed by $\ell^n$, for every $n\geq1$. Apply the finite-ring assertion just proved to $C_n$ with this ring. The same geometric fibre bound $d$ and the given common input interval $[a,b]$ give $[a,b+2d]$ independently of $n$. The input tower lies in $D^+(\operatorname{Tow})$, as required for the levelwise comparison: by [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], kernels and cokernels are formed levelwise (the induced transition maps descend to the component kernels and quotients). Therefore cohomology is computed levelwise, and vanishing of every $\mathcal H^q(C_n)$ for $q<a$ makes the cohomology tower zero in those degrees. Clause (1) of [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels] identifies $(Rf_{!,\bullet}C_\bullet)_n$ with $Rf_{!,A_n}C_n$. Thus these are the asserted common Tor bounds for the tower levels. In the definition [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], the test module $N=A_n$ is the tensor unit, so each output level itself has cohomology only in $[a,b+2d]$. No compatibility of new projection maps is claimed or needed here.

source.place: Final sentence: apply the finite-ring bound levelwise, then test with the coefficient ring
